analysis:
MARKET & REGIME: SPY is MIXED — marginally below SMA50 but with a rising 20-day slope. This is not the time to press new exposure. Remain cautious and let the existing book breathe.

PORTFOLIO REVIEW:
• A (Agilent, +7.73%): Best performer. Now 64% of 52w range, +8.9% above SMA50 — entering extended territory. Thesis intact (life-science tools recovery, solid margins). Trail stop mentally to protect gains; do not chase add.
• AMP (-0.10%): Essentially at breakeven. Insurance/wealth management quality. Thesis in early innings — watching for a catalyst. No action needed yet.
• CI (-3.10%): Managed care under persistent sector pressure (rate uncertainty, MLR headwinds). Down but not yet at stop; keep watching. If sector deterioration continues, stop discipline must hold.
• FDS (-5.20%): Entry $259.70, now ~$244–246. FDS reappears as the screener's top-ranked basing candidate (25% of 52w range, fwd P/E 12.4, PEG 1.10, ROE 27%, $621M FCF). The fundamentals are sound and the base is forming, but averaging into a losing position requires extra caution. Not adding here given we already hold it at a loss — let price confirm the base first. A weekly close above $250 with volume would be constructive; a close below $238 (approximately 2x ATR below current) breaks the thesis and triggers exit.
• LII (-6.55%): Weakest position. HVAC is cyclical and macro-sensitive. Entry $575.57, now $537.89. This is approaching the -7 to -8% range where a properly set 1.5–2x ATR stop should trigger. If not already formally set, the stop should sit near $530–$535 (approximately 7.3–7.7% below entry). Honor it without hesitation if hit.

CAPACITY: At 5 positions (the maximum for this 3–5 concentrated strategy), there is no room for a new long without closing one. Headroom is $32K but adding a 6th position violates the concentration rule.

PERFORMANCE HONESTY: Win rate 41.7%, profit factor 0.95x, Sortino -5.79. These numbers say plainly that there is no demonstrated stock-picking edge here vs. a passive SPY blend. The WDAY saga (3 stop-hits on the same name) is a textbook reminder that re-entering a falling knife costs real money. The correct response is a higher bar for new entries, not more activity.

NEW CANDIDATES REVIEW: Several candidates are genuinely interesting — MCO (ROE 77%, Op margin 49%, basing at 49% of range, 89 days to earnings), VEEV (PEG 0.85, 16% rev growth, 18% of range, but earnings in 40 days = elevated risk), ZBRA/BKNG/ZBH/WDC all have earnings within 12 days (avoid). MU, WDC, AMAT, HPE are all extended well above SMA200 (late-cycle risk). PAYX is already 9.5% above SMA50. None of these justify forcing a 6th position. MCO is the standout watchlist name — if LII or FDS stops out naturally, MCO is the highest-conviction replacement candidate (basing, exceptional quality, long runway to earnings).

DECISION: Zero new trades. Preserve capital, honor stops on LII and FDS if triggered, protect gains in A. Cash at 37% is appropriate insurance in a mixed tape with a book that's still finding its footing. A quiet, disciplined week is a success.
